narrative: 大多数场景都活在中景里，因为人们说话时会用手比划。一只杯子、一部电话、一支烟、一本被摔在桌上的笔记本，都发生在腰部到脸之间的这段空间里。
环境信息依然会露出一点（一个卡座、一扇窗、一道门），但不会成为主体。当故事是一段行走、一整套从头到脚的装束，或者一张必须成为唯一风景的脸时，中景就不是合适的工具。
如果你从不离开这个景别，调度就会变成一出只有脑袋和腰带的广播剧。当腰线已经容纳不下你想表达的事实时，就该换景别了。
how: 画面下边缘卡在腰部或腰带处，静止时的双手应该留在画面里。
在对话时常见的站立或坐姿距离上，用40mm到50mm镜头能保持透视的自然感；教科书式的50mm只是一个默认值，不是铁律。摄影机通常架在胸部到眼睛的高度。
你依然应该能读到一点场景信息，而不是整个房间的地图。提示词：Medium shot of [Subject] from the waist up, gesture and face in balance.
when: 把它当作日常主力覆盖镜头使用：交叠的对话、卡座里的交谈、有人拎着行李箱把手在画面里等待。当关键信息是髋部以下的枪套、脚，或者需要更近裁切才能看清的微表情时，不要用它。
vs: 中近景（Medium Close-Up）从胸部开始，舍弃腰部；牛仔镜头（Cowboy Shot）把下边缘降到大腿中部，好让手停在枪套那条线上时依然在画面里。
中景说的是“腰部”这句话，既不是中近景，也不是牛仔镜头。特写则完全是另一句话：脸的优先级高于手势。
examples_film: 《满城风雨》（His Girl Friday）把对话和手势都放在这个景别区间里运作，让交叠的台词依然带着香烟、电话和办公桌。《迷失东京》（Lost in Translation）用腰部以上的酒店和酒吧距离，让两个人可以共存，既不沦为肖像特写，也不变成空旷的全景地图。
mistakes: 最常被搞混的近邻是牛仔镜头（膝盖或大腿中部入画）或中近景（腰带消失）。破绽是要么出现了枪带，要么胸部悬浮在画面里没有下文。
解决办法：在腰部裁切。另一个破绽是把每一个说话的画面都叫作中景，其实它是中近景。

faq.q: What is Medium Shot in film?
faq.a: 中景通常把人物从腰部以上纳入画面，让脸和手势共享同一个画面。它是一个景别，有时也被称为“腰部镜头”，是很多场景覆盖的默认景别。
牛仔镜头从大腿中部或膝盖以上取景，让垂下的手和枪套那条线保留在画面里。中景则在腰部裁切，腰带以下的一切都被排除在外。如果你能看到大腿，那就不是中景。

faq.q: When should I use Medium Shot?
faq.a: 当说话和手上的动作就是这场戏的重点时使用它：桌子、电话、杯子、笔记。当你需要拍脚、枪带、整套装束，或者一张没有躯干的脸时，不要用它。

faq.q: How do I prompt Medium Shot for AI image or video?
faq.a: 写：Medium shot of [Subject] from the waist up, conversational distance, 50mm。保持双手在画面里。不要写“牛仔”“全身”或“胸部以上”。

narrative: Most scenes live in the medium shot because people talk with their hands. A glass, a phone, a cigarette, a slammed notebook all happen between waist and face.

Geography is still a little present (a booth, a window, a doorway) without becoming the subject. It is the wrong tool when the story is a walk, a costume from head to toe, or a face that must be the only landscape.
If you never leave this size, blocking becomes a radio play with heads and belts. Change size when the waist line no longer contains the fact.
how: Bottom frame at the waist or belt. Hands at rest should be in.
A 40mm to 50mm at conversational standing or sitting distance keeps perspective ordinary; the catalog 50mm is a default, not a law. Camera often at chest to eye height.
You should still read a bit of set, not a full room map. Prompt: Medium shot of [Subject] from the waist up, gesture and face in balance.
when: Use it as workhorse coverage: overlapping dialogue, a booth conversation, someone waiting with a suitcase handle in frame. Do not use it when the information is a holster below the hip, the feet, or a micro-expression that needs a closer crop.
vs: A Medium Close-Up starts at the chest and throws the waist away. A Cowboy Shot drops the bottom frame to mid-thigh so hands at the holster line stay in.
Medium is the waist sentence, not MCU and not cowboy. A Close-Up is a different sentence entirely: the face outranks gesture.
examples_film: His Girl Friday runs talk and gesture in this band so overlapping dialogue still has cigarettes, phones, and desks. Lost in Translation uses waist-up hotel and bar distance where two people can exist without becoming portraits or wide maps.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a Cowboy Shot (knees or mid-thigh in) or a Medium Close-Up (belt gone). The tell is either a gunbelt or a floating chest.
Fix: crop at the waist. Another tell is calling every talky frame a medium shot when it is an MCU.

faq.q: What is Medium Shot in film?
faq.a: A medium shot usually frames a person from the waist up so face and gesture share the frame. It is a size, sometimes called a waist shot, and it is the default band for a lot of scene coverage.

A cowboy shot frames from mid-thigh or the knees up so hanging hands and a holster line remain. A medium shot cuts at the waist, so anything below the belt is out. If you can see thigh, you are not in a medium shot.

faq.q: When should I use Medium Shot?
faq.a: Use it when talk and hand business are the scene: tables, phones, glasses, notes. Do not use it when you need feet, a gunbelt, a full costume, or a face with no torso.

faq.q: How do I prompt Medium Shot for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write Medium shot of [Subject] from the waist up, conversational distance, 50mm. Keep hands in. Do not say cowboy, full body, or chest up.
